source_document.body:
EIB and IDC officials sign the financing agreement on Thursday, Nov. 26. Credit: European Investment Bank.
By: Northern Miner Staff November 27, 2026
The European Investment Bank (EIB) and South Africa’s Industrial Development Corporation (IDC) agreed to jointly provide up to €300 million (US$327 million) to advance African critical minerals projects, linking investment in local processing and industry with Europe’s efforts to diversify supplies.
Announced Thursday, the facility is expected to support around €900 million in total investment, according to the EIB. It’s consistent with South Africa’s 2025 Critical Minerals Strategy , which aims to process more minerals locally and expand the country’s role in supplying global industries.
“Ultimately, this facility is about turning our mineral wealth into factories, skills and jobs,” IDC CEO Mmakgoshi Lekhethe said in a statement .
By enabling investment in strategic minerals and related industries, the financing “will contribute to economic growth, value creation and greater supply chain resilience for both Africa and Europe,” added EIB Vice-President Ambroise Fayolle, who signed the agreement on behalf of the Luxembourg-based lender.
Eligible activities range from extraction and processing to refining, recycling and substitution, along with supporting energy, transport and digital infrastructure. Projects in South Africa and other sub-Saharan African countries must contribute to local industrial development and demonstrate a clear connection to European value chains, the EIB said.
Access to capital
For developers, infrastructure funding could help address financing needs that extend beyond the boundaries of a mine or a processing plant.
The deal addresses a major obstacle to developing the continent’s mineral resources: access to long-term capital at competitive prices. Its emphasis on beneficiation and downstream processing aims to build local industrial capacity and employment while attracting other investors into projects, according to the IDC.
The facility is the EIB’s first dedicated critical minerals financing operation outside the European Union under the strategic initiative it launched in 2025. The announcement didn’t identify project recipients or disclose individual loan allocations. Projects are expected to meet international environmental and social standards.
Close to home
South Africa’s critical minerals and metals strategy calls for more exploration, processing close to mines, power and infrastructure investments as well as financial instruments, according to the mineral resources department.
The strategy also prioritizes research, skills and regional integration. Its industrial objective is to increase the value retained from mineral production through stronger domestic manufacturing and a broader export base, rather than relying principally on overseas processing, the department’s announcement explained.
The new financing follows a November 2025 accord between the European Union and South Africa on sustainable minerals and metals value chains. That partnership was signed alongside a clean trade and investment agreement, placing minerals within a wider effort to strengthen industrial links and investment between the two economies, according to the European Council.
Africa focus
The EIB has already backed preparatory work elsewhere in Africa. In February, it announced agreements offering Andrada Mining and EcoGraf up to €2 million each in technical assistance.
The support covers Andrada’s expansion into lithium in Namibia and EcoGraf’s natural graphite development in Tanzania, including engineering, infrastructure and environmental work to improve investment readiness.
Friday’s announcement extends a busy week for the bank’s minerals financing. On Wednesday, the EIB agreed to invest about €400 million in Polish miner KGHM to support deeper copper deposits, underground transport and processing upgrades, reinforcing its parallel push to secure production within Europe.
